claims.text: The initial FeCoNi alloy has an FCC structure.
The proposed intervention is to replace a fraction of Fe in FeCoNi with Cr.
The resulting alloy can retain an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Substitution of Cr for Fe will cause formation of a mixed FCC and BCC structure.
The BCC phase has higher coercivity.
Cr substitution will change the magnetic properties of the alloy.
Cr substitution will increase magnetic anisotropy.
Increased magnetic anisotropy will produce higher coercivity.
The Cr-modified FeCoNi-based alloy will have higher coercivity than FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt.
The intervention should apply only while the resulting material remains an almost equiatomic high-entropy alloy with configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
The amount of Cr substitution needed to obtain the desired coercivity is uncertain.

contradictions.description: If FeCoNi denotes the usual equiatomic ternary, replacing only part of Fe with Cr gives Co and Ni fractions near one third while Fe and Cr divide the remaining third; no substitution fraction makes all four elements approximately equiatomic. The single substitution intervention is therefore difficult to reconcile with the stated almost-equiatomic quaternary constraint.

The prediction uses FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt as the comparison baseline, whereas the falsification rule asks only whether coercivity increases with Cr substitution. An increase relative to an unsubstituted composition need not exceed the named prior derivatives, so the experimental decision rule does not test the stated comparative outcome decisively.
